### Two things worth your attention

**1. A performance defect in the planned email pattern, found and fixed.** The pattern as written in research D-001/T011 scans in **O(n²)** on line length: the greedy local part matches to end of line, then backtracks a character at a time hunting for `@`, at *every* start offset. Measured 0.42 s on a 16 KB line — the 1 MB line that quickstart Scenario 5 explicitly requires would have taken roughly half an hour. The Phase 0 throughput probe missed it because it only used short lines.

I added a derived leading guard, `(?<![A-Za-z0-9._%+\-])`, directly analogous to D-002's derived `(?<!\d\.)`. It accepts exactly the same strings — `@` is not in the local-part class, so every offset inside one run reaches the same `@` and the same domain, meaning a match from mid-run implies a match from the run's first character, which leftmost-first precedence (FR-017) already prefers. 1 MB line now takes 0.13 s. The reasoning is recorded in a comment at the pattern; `research.md` does not yet mention it.

**2. FR-022's permission-denied case cannot be provoked as root.** Root bypasses permission bits, so `chmod 000` does not raise `PermissionError`. Rather than leave FR-022's mapped test reporting SKIPPED (which would mean an FR without a *passing* test), the three provokable causes — missing, directory, undecodable — always assert in `test_fr022_...`, and a companion `test_fr022_permission_denied_names_path_and_exits_2` asserts the denied case strictly, skipped only when it cannot be provoked. I verified it genuinely passes by re-running those tests as the unprivileged `nobody` user.
